title: API key binding drift during rollout causes intermittent 401/403 and audit log misattribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers (hosted and Dedicated) reported intermittent 401/403 responses during a canary rollout of the API key signing service. Side-effects include incorrect org attribution in audit logs and temporary inability to access routes that should be allowed for valid API keys. The issue is reproducible during rolling deploys when the mapping cache update propagates unevenly across edge proxies.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy new version of api-key-signer to 10% of nodes (canary) while leaving rest at v1
Issue a fresh API key bind request for org 'acme-corp' using the signer v2 pathway
Concurrently send requests through multiple edge proxies with cached mappings (mix of v1/v2 aware caches)
Observe intermittent 401/403 for the same API key depending on edge node and short-term cache state
Check audit logs: some requests show org 'acme-corp', others show 'unknown' or a stale org id
impact_summary: Customers experienced production outages up to 5 minutes per window, with several support escalations for Dedicated and Private deployments. Revenue-impacting customers saw degraded features and increased support load. Audit trails were partially inconsistent during the window, complicating post-incident forensics.
timeline: 2026-03-10 09:03 UTC - First alert from monitoring: spike in 401 rate for api.gateway.prod across region us-west-2
2026-03-10 09:11 UTC - Support ticket from Dedicated customer reporting inability to call embeddings endpoints (escalated)
2026-03-10 09:27 UTC - On-call triage confirms correlation with api-key-signer canary rollout
2026-03-10 09:40 UTC - Mitigation applied: paused rollout and applied fallback that accepts last-known-bindings for 60s
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - 401 rate returns to baseline; customers notified; postmortem task opened
mitigation: Rollback canary to v1 and enable conservative acceptance window on gateway (accept last-known-binding for 60s after cache invalidation). Added temporary alert for binding-mismatch ratio > 0.5% per minute. Communicated to customers and reopened onboarding ticket for affected orgs.
root_cause: Race condition in the api-key-binding reconciler + edge cache invalidation path. v2 introduced a non-idempotent bind handler that updated the mapping without bumping a global binding_version. Edge proxies use local caches keyed by (api_key, binding_version). During rollout some nodes served v2-generated bindings with implicit defaults, while others still validated against v1 semantics, producing transient mismatch and authn failures. Additionally, audit-log writer used best-effort org resolution and sometimes logged 'unknown' when mapping not available.
fix_details: 1) Make bind handler idempotent and always increment an explicit binding_version stored alongside the api_key mapping in the central store. 2) Add a compare-and-swap (CAS) update to prevent concurrent writers from leaving partial state. 3) Publish invalidation events to the global pubsub (kafka topic 'apikey-bindings-v') and ensure proxies subscribe and apply versioned invalidation. 4) Update audit-logger to fallback to last-resolved org with a note rather than 'unknown' to preserve forensic trails. 5) Add integration tests that simulate rolling upgrades and multi-proxy traffic patterns.
rollout_plan:
1) Ship DB migration to add 'binding_version' (backwards-compatible default 1) in canary (auth-2026.03.1-migrate).
2) Deploy signer v2 with CAS + version bump behind feature flag to 5% canary for 24 hours with tight monitoring.
3) Enable pubsub invalidation on proxies in a phased manner (canary proxies first).
4) Gradually increase to 25% and then 100% if no errors.
5) After full rollout, remove fallback acceptance window in next release.
follow_up_tasks: Add e2e chaos test for rolling deploys in CI that asserts auth stability
Create runbook entry for binding drift incidents and include quick rollback steps
Add SLO for binding-mismatch ratio and dashboard tile in Redwood Console
Complete security review and KMS compatibility check for binding_version migration
Perform audit log reconciliation for affected customers and send detailed incident report
